title: Run MD cascade simulations
action: Perform molecular dynamics simulations of displacement cascades in 3C‑SiC using LAMMPS with a Tersoff potential. Create a periodic 3C‑SiC lattice at 300 K and initiate cascades by giving a randomly chosen Si atom a velocity corresponding to damage energies of 0.25, 0.5, 1, 5, 10, and 30 keV along crystallographic directions. Use system sizes appropriate to the energy (8000 atoms for low energies, up to 2 million atoms for 30 keV) with damping boundaries. Run at least 5 cascades per energy for energies ≥ 1 keV, and at least 15 for energies < 1 keV. Save atomic trajectories for subsequent analysis.

title: Compute cascade lifetime for 10 keV Si PKA
action: From the saved trajectory of one 10 keV Si PKA cascade, identify atoms displaced more than half the nearest‑neighbour distance from their lattice site. Compute the mean‑square displacement (MSD) of these atoms as a function of time and determine the cascade lifetime as the characteristic relaxation time (time after which MSD levels off). Write the lifetime in picoseconds to a text file.
description: Single float representing the cascade lifetime (in picoseconds) for a 10 keV Si primary knock‑on atom in 3C‑SiC.
output_schema: A single non‑negative number on the first line, e.g., 0.15

title: Compute defect production efficiency, Frenkel pair ratio, and anti‑site fraction
action: For all Si PKA cascades at each damage energy (0.25, 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 30 keV), identify displaced atoms, vacancies, interstitials, and anti‑site defects after cascade relaxation. Count total displacements as the sum of Frenkel pairs and anti‑site defects, and count anti‑site defects. For each energy, compute defect production efficiency as N_displacements / (0.4 * E_PKA / E_d) using a weighted average displacement threshold energy E_d = 22 eV, and the anti‑site defect fraction as N_anti_site / N_displacements. For the 10 keV Si PKA cascades, report the ratio of C interstitials to Si interstitials. Output a JSON file summarising these per‑energy results.
description: Object with keys for each damage energy (0.25, 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 30) containing total_displacements (float), efficiency (float), anti_site_fraction (float), and for the 10 keV entry additionally ratio_C_Si_interstitials (float).

title: Report largest interstitial cluster size
action: From the defect identification in step 03, determine the largest interstitial cluster (connected group of interstitial atoms within nearest‑neighbour distance) observed across all cascades. Write the integer size (number of interstitials in that cluster) to a text file.
description: A single integer representing the maximum number of interstitials in any cluster observed over all simulated cascades.
output_schema: One non‑negative integer on the first line, e.g., 3
